articles.title: DJ Moore injury sparks surprise Bills suggestion as former NFL star names 9,811-yard WR as potential replacement
articles.summary: NFL News: The Buffalo Bills beat the Detroit Lions in their new stadium opener, but the win came with a cost. Wide receiver DJ Moore left the game in the second.
articles.body: The Buffalo Bills beat the Detroit Lions in their new stadium opener, but the win came with a cost. Wide receiver DJ Moore left the game in the second quarter with a shoulder stinger and never came back. Moore was ruled out for the remainder of the game, and with his status now uncertain heading into next week, the conversation has quickly shifted to who Buffalo might turn to if he misses time. Former NFL cornerback Darius Butler already has a name in mind, and it is one that Bills fans will recognize.Could Brandin Cooks be the answer if DJ Moore misses games?Butler posted on X that Brandin Cooks is going to be a Buffalo Bill by Sunday. He is speculating, but the suggestion is not without logic. Cooks visited the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday, which means he is clearly open to returning to the NFL. And the Bills, who know him well, could very much come calling.Cooks is 33 now and has not played this season, but the resume speaks for itself. Over 12 NFL seasons with the Saints, Patriots, Rams, Texans, Cowboys, and yes, the Bills, he has put up 9,811 receiving yards, 734 receptions, and 60 touchdowns across 173 games. Buffalo signed him last year, and though he only played five games, catching five passes for 114 yards, he still knows the offense and the culture around the building.The Bills did not trade a second-round pick to Chicago for Moore just to replace him with a stopgap. Moore was supposed to be Josh Allen's true No. 1 receiver, the kind Buffalo has not really had since Stefon Diggs was dealt to Houston before the 2024 season. So if Moore misses meaningful time, the pressure on everyone else goes up, not just on a potential free agent addition.How big is DJ Moore's absence for the Buffalo Bills offense?Moore's first two games as a Bill told you everything about why they wanted him. In Week 1 against the Texans, he caught five balls for 100 yards and a touchdown. Head coach Joe Brady was direct about what Moore brings. "Yeah, I mean, you see there's a reason we brought him here and the ability that he can make plays down the field. And look, we had a pass interference that's not even going to show up in the stat book, right? But that's another added bonus, right? You saw the different types of weapons that we had, with DJ having a big game, Dalton [Kincaid] had a big game," Brady said on Monday, via A to Z Sports.Kincaid has been genuinely good through two weeks. He caught five passes for 130 yards against Houston and followed that with seven catches for 95 yards and a score against Detroit. He can carry more load. But Moore's value goes beyond catch counts. His ability to draw pass interference, threaten deep, and move the chains on third down is not something you just replace with a name off the street.That is what makes the Cooks idea interesting rather than just a throwaway suggestion. He has been in those moments before. He understands what a No. 1 receiver is supposed to do in a system like this. Whether he can still do it at his age is the question Buffalo would need to answer quickly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sean McVay hopes Rams never play in Australia 'ever again'
articles.summary: McVay enjoyed the atmosphere Down Under, but is happy to return to a normal schedule of preparation.
articles.body:
It would make Sean McVay very happy if the Los Angeles Rams avoided playing in Australia again while he is head coach.

The Rams' much-talked-about trip Down Under ended in a 27-7 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers last week. It was a game to forget for McVay.

"I want to see us be present right now and move forward," McVay said Thursday . "That game is so far — it's almost like you try to do the 'Men in Black' thing where you say, 'Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago.' We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context."

There were over 100,000 fans in attendance at the Melbourne Cricket Ground for the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Australia. It won't be the last time the league makes the trip as Brett Gosper, the NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, told the Australian Financial Review that there will be at least two more games over the next three seasons.

As McVay said, his sour experience had nothing to do with the country itself or everything outside of the game. As 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan this week said, it was tough to enjoy it all when you're focused on working.

The Rams head coach was back in his comfortable place this week: back home in Los Angeles as the team goes through a normal week of preparation as they host the New York Giants on Monday night .

"Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let's go be about it," McVay said. "Let's go prepare the right way. Let's have great focus and concentration. Let's have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let's go be ready to go against a really damn good football team.

"What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That's what every week is. We're excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today."

articles.title: 3 things to know from Seattle Seahawks' Week 1 win
articles.summary: The Cardinals host the Seahawks in Week 2. What can we learn from Seattle's season-opening win?
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will be at home in Week 2 facing the defending champion Seattle Seahawks . The Cardinals are coming off a Week 1 26-14 upset win over the Los Angeles Chargers . The Seahawks rallied from down 10-0 to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 behind backup quarterback Drew Lock , who entered the game after Sam Darnold exited in the first quarter with a gluteal injury.

What can the Cardinals expect from the Seahawks in Week 2? There are three things to know from the Seahawks' Week 1 win.

They picked off Patriots quarterback Drake Maye three times in Week 1, all three times in the fourth quarter. And the Seahawks capitalized, scoring after the first two takeaways to take the lead and then running the clock out after the final interception in the end zone.

They do not allow running backs to get yards

The Patriots rushed for 109 yards, but 47 of those came from Maye scrambling. Seattle's defense held Rhamondre Stevenson and former Cardinal Corey Kiner to 62 yards on 24 attempts, an average of 2.6 yards per carry.

Receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was last season's Offensive Player of the Year, and he started the season dominant. He had eight receptions for 122 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. He is their top target. The Seahawks attempted 24 passes in Week 1. Eleven were thrown JSN's way.

articles.title: Updated NFL MVP odds after Josh Allen’s epic 5 touchdown performance
articles.summary: Josh Allen accounted for five touchdowns against the Detroit Lions on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Josh Allen is the favorite to win NFL MVP. It still very early in the season, but he's on pace for the type of historic season that we've only really seen from Patrick Mahomes and Peyton Manning during seasons they won the award and took their teams deep into the postseason.

Allen was the favorite after Week 1 and a dominant performance against the Detroit Lions in the Bills' first game at Highmark Stadium only increased his lead over Lamar Jackson . After his five touchdown game on Thursday Night Football Allen moved from +475 to +260.

While Allen's big night didn't affect Lamar Jackson's odds much, if at all, it did make Caleb Williams drop from +750 to +1100.

MVP odds after Josh Allen's Thursday night performance: Josh Allen +260 Lamar Jackson +650 Caleb Williams +1100 Patrick Mahomes +1200 Trevor Lawrence +1300 pic.twitter.com/BdwqUBYAA4 — PFF (@PFF) September 18, 2026

MVP odds after Josh Allen's Thursday night performance: Josh Allen +260 Lamar Jackson +650 Caleb Williams +1100 Patrick Mahomes +1200 Trevor Lawrence +1300 pic.twitter.com/BdwqUBYAA4

Jackson, Williams and the rest of the betting favorites will get a chance to respond on Sunday.

While Allen is on pace for a huge year, Williams and Jackson had huge season openers as well. Jackson threw for 324 yards and a touchdown and ran for another touchdown while Williams had his own Allen-esque two touchdowns rushing and passing to go along with 265 yards passing and 65 yards rushing.

The Bears will host the Minnesota Vikings at 1 p.m. ET. Jackson and the Ravens will also host the New Orleans Saints in the early window. The next chance for either of those quarterbacks to make a statement in primetime will come in Week 3 when the Bears host the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football. The Ravens will play on Sunday Night Football in Week 5.
